newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SELES SAILS INTO TOSHIBA CLASSIC SEMIFINALS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SELES SAILS INTO TOSHIBA CLASSIC SEMIFINALS.

text.p: Second seed Monica Seles showed some flashes of the form that once made her the world's top tennis player Thursday as she sailed into the semifinals of the Toshiba Tennis Classic.
Seles, who has reached three finals this year but has yet to add to her 38 career singles titles, overpowered doubles star Natasha Zvereva of Belarus 6-1 6-3.
"In terms of effort it was really good," said the third-ranked Seles after the one hour and 20 minute match.
"I wasn't giving up today and that's what I really wanted coming into the match," added Seles, who has struggled with her form and consistency all year.

Seles unleashed her punishing ground attack and ran down Zvereva's numerous drop shots in the first meeting beteen the two. The second seed was also helped by Zvereva's 33 unforced while commiting just 13 herself.
"She definitely was hitting the ball hard. She jumps on every opportunity," noted Zvereva, who has been a member of the winning doubles team in all three Grand Slam events this year.
Seles will likely be more severely tested Saturday by third-seeded South African Amanda Coetzer, who reached her ninth semifinal of the year.
Coetzer combined patience with power to beat Indonesian Yayuk Basuki 6-3 6-4 in an earlier quarter-final.
"I played the right shot at the right time. I didn't try to go for two much," the seventh-ranked Coetzer said.

Basuki, who was coming off Wednesday's upset of fifth seed Anke Huber, actually hit 16 more winners than Coetzer. But her 33 unforced errors -- compared to just 11 for the South African -- nullified all her good work.
"She can be a very dangerous but I was the steadier player today," said Coetzer, who has two wins over Steffi Graf under her belt this year.
Earlier Thursday, seventh seed Conchita Martinez romped into the quarter-finals with a 46-minute, 6-1 6-0 pasting of Czech veteran Helena Sukova.
"It was a great match for me. I was very aggressive and didn't let her play her game," said the 1994 Wimbledon champion.

Martinez will not have long to savor her lopsided victory. The win put the Spaniard directly in the path of world number one Martina Hingis just days after the Swiss teen crushed Martinez in a final at Palo Alto.
In Friday's other quarter-final, sixth seed Mary Pierce faces French compatriot Sandrine Testud, who surprised fourth-seeded Spaniard Arantxa Sanchez Vicario on Wednesday.
